dataUsage.howMeasuredBody: Dishylink integrates the dish's own per-second throughput telemetry into per-minute volume, on this machine. It tracks your real traffic from the moment the historian started — it is not Starlink's billing meter, which lives in their cloud and counts in UTC.

merge.explanation: This device appears twice, both named <name>{{name}}</name>. This happens when a device changes its Wi-Fi address and your router treats it as new.

connect.title: Connect your Starlink account
connect.signInPitch: See your plan, data usage, service address, and every dish and router on the account, and enable supported router controls such as pausing connected devices. Your session stays encrypted on this device and is only ever sent to Starlink.
connect.signInNote: A Starlink login window opens — nothing is shared with anyone but Starlink.
connect.pastePitch: Adds account details and supported router controls. The session is written to a local .starlink-cookie file on this machine and only ever sent to Starlink.
connect.step1: In a new tab, sign in at <link>starlink.com/account</link>.
connect.step2: Open DevTools (F12 / ⌥⌘I) and switch to the Network tab.
connect.step3: Reload the page, then click any request to starlink.com in the list.
connect.step4: Under Request Headers, find cookie: and copy its entire value.
connect.step5: Paste it below and Connect. (Don't use the console's document.cookie — it drops the part we need.)

account.required: An authorized account is required — <link>sign in</link> to use this feature.

obstruction.obstructedNote: Obstructed patches cause brief interruptions as satellites pass behind them.

obstruction.next30MinTip: The fewest serviceable satellites at any moment over the next 30 minutes, from SpaceX's published orbits. A low number can mean brief drops as satellites hand off.
obstruction.likelyServingTip: Our best guess at the satellite your dish is talking to right now — the highest, unobstructed one, inferred from live orbits.

bypass.title: Bypass mode
bypass.tip: Advanced feature that disables the Starlink router completely, so the dish serves a third-party router instead. The Starlink WiFi goes off and the client list, custom DNS and subnet stop working. Most users should leave this off.
bypass.sentUnconfirmable: Sent. This device can't reach your Starlink account now, so nothing here can confirm it.
bypass.couldNotConfirm: Couldn't confirm the change from here. Reopen this panel to check again.
bypass.connectInternetAndSignIn: Connect this device to the internet and sign in your account to use
bypass.unknownState: Couldn't tell whether the router is bypassed
bypass.onCaption: The Starlink router is disabled; a third-party router runs the network
bypass.offCaption: The Starlink router is running your network
bypass.sentOn: Sent. The Starlink WiFi is going down; waiting for the account to confirm.
bypass.sentOff: Sent! The router is coming back up; waiting for confirmation…
bypass.slideOn: Slide to turn on bypass mode
bypass.slideOff: Slide to turn off bypass mode
bypass.explainOff: Bypass mode will completely disable the Starlink router and its WiFi. Only a third-party router wired to the dish stays online. You can turn it back off from here as long as this device has access to the internet.
bypass.explainOn: Bypass is on, so the Starlink router is disabled and a third-party router runs your network. Turning bypass off brings the Starlink router and its WiFi back.
bypass.explainUnknown: Can't tell whether bypass is on. Turning it off is the safe direction either way: it brings the Starlink router and its WiFi back, and changes nothing if bypass was already off.
bypass.confirmOn: The Starlink router and its WiFi will switch off. Only devices behind a third-party router wired to the dish stay online. You can turn bypass back off from here as long as this device still has internet — if nothing else provides it, you will need another device on mobile data.
bypass.confirmOff: The Starlink router and its WiFi come back on. Devices connected through a third-party router may need to reconnect.

subnet.title: Subnet
subnet.tip: Advanced feature that changes the IP addresses assigned to your devices. Most users should use the default. Changing it drops the network for up to a minute while every device is issued a new address.
subnet.passwordTip: Entering the wrong password here overrides your current password and no device can rejoin the WiFi until you set back the correct password in the official Starlink mobile app.
subnet.moving: Moving to {{subnet}}. Reconnect to the WiFi if this device drops.
subnet.unknown: Couldn't tell which subnet the router is on
subnet.caption: The address range the router gives your devices
subnet.confirmBody: The network drops for up to a minute while every device is issued a new address. If the password is wrong, nothing can rejoin the WiFi until you retype it in the official Starlink app.

routerDiagnosis.addressTaken: Another device on this network is using {{address}}, the address the Starlink router answers on, so the router is hidden behind it. To fix it, connect to your Starlink WiFi, give the other router a different address (like {{alternative}}), or point Dishylink's router address at wherever your Starlink router actually is.

routerDiagnosis.bypassed: Bypass mode is on, so the Starlink router is switched off and a third-party router runs your network. WiFi, the client list and the router's own settings all come from it, so there's nothing to show here. Everything on the dish is unaffected.
routerDiagnosis.noRouter: The dish isn't reporting a Starlink router, so this kit either doesn't have one or it's powered off. WiFi and connected devices come from the router, so there's nothing to show here. Everything on the dish is unaffected.
routerDiagnosis.unknown: Couldn't reach the Starlink router at {{address}}. Another device may be using that address, the router may be in bypass mode or on a different network, or it may be at an address other than the one Dishylink is set to use.
routerDiagnosis.checking: Couldn't reach the Starlink router at {{address}}. Working out why; most short silences are the router restarting.

dns.title: Custom DNS
dns.tip: Custom DNS lets you specify IPv4 or IPv6 addresses of one or more alternate DNS servers to be used for lookups instead of the Starlink defaults. A server that doesn't answer stops lookups for every device on the network.
dns.caption: Send name lookups to your own servers instead of Starlink's

alignment.stale: Dish not answering — showing the last reading.
alignment.staleFrom: Dish not answering — showing the last reading from {{when}}.
alignment.notReady: Attitude filter not ready — alignment data is settling.
alignment.aligned: Starlink is aligned — pointed in the correct direction.
alignment.notAligned: Starlink is not aligned — adjust the dish toward the wedge.
alignment.noReading: Couldn't reach the Starlink dish — alignment needs a live reading. This updates on its own once the dish is back online.
alignment.currentRotationHint: Current rotation (boresight azimuth) is the compass direction the dish is actually pointing, measured clockwise from North (0° to 360°).
alignment.rotateRecommendationHint: How far to turn the dish around, and which way, seen from above. ↺ is anticlockwise, ↻ is clockwise.
alignment.targetAzimuthHint: The compass direction the dish wants to point, clockwise from North, and how far either side of it still counts as aligned.
alignment.boresightErrorHint: Boresight error (pointing error) is how far the dish is pointing from where it wants to point, as one angle. Under {{limit}}° counts as aligned.
alignment.attitudeUncertaintyHint: How sure the dish is of its own orientation. Smaller is better — a large figure means the readings above are still settling.
alignment.attitudeStateHint: Whether the dish has finished working out its own orientation. Converged means the alignment figures can be trusted.
alignment.gpsSatellitesHint: GPS satellites the dish can currently see. It uses these to fix its own position and orientation, not for the internet link.
alignment.currentTiltHint: Current tilt (tilt angle) is the physical angle of the dish plate off flat. Flat is 0°, and the steeper the plate the lower it aims.
alignment.tiltRecommendationHint: How far to re-aim the dish up or down, and which way. Down means the dish is aiming too high; steepen the plate to bring it down.
alignment.boresightElevationHint: Boresight elevation is how far above the horizon the dish is actually pointing, where 0° is level with the horizon and 90° is straight up.
alignment.targetElevationHint: Target elevation is the angle above the horizon this dish wants to point, worked out for your location.
alignment.elevationRangeHint: Acceptable elevation range is the span of elevations that still counts as aligned. It is the grey wedge drawn on the Tilt dial above — while the dish points inside it, the dial stays green.
alignment.hasActuatorsHint: Whether the dish steers itself with motors. Without them, aiming is electronic and any physical adjustment is done by hand.
alignment.actuationStateHint: What the dish’s motors are doing right now — idle, or actively moving to a new position.
alignment.howToReadBody: The wedge shows the desired pointing direction ± tolerance. The dish plate and orange needle show where the dish is actually pointing. If the needle is inside the wedge, the dish is aligned. If it’s outside, adjust the dish toward the wedge. Values update live every 2s

latencyQuality.explainer: Latency quality summarizes the period as a single 0–100 score with a letter grade, weighing typical latency, jitter, worst-case spikes, and packet loss together rather than just the average. A connection that's mostly fast but occasionally stutters scores lower than one that's a little slower but steady, since that unevenness is what you'd actually notice in a game, a call, or a video stream.

metrics.dishNotAnswering: dish isn’t answering — no status received yet
metrics.waitingForDish: waiting for the dish’s first reply…
metrics.energyUsedFull: energy used over the selected window
metrics.energyUsedMinutes: energy used recorded {{count}} min of this window

metrics.energyUsedNothing: energy used nothing recorded in this window

metrics.routerPingNote: the router's own pings to its point of presence, over a rolling five minutes

metrics.downloadExplainer: Download throughput is the rate data arrives from the internet to your dish, in bits per second. It spikes while you're actively pulling data and idles near zero when nothing is downloading.
metrics.uploadExplainer: Upload throughput is the rate data leaves your dish for the internet. It's typically much lower than download and rises when you send large files, back up data, or make video calls.
metrics.latencyExplainer: The Starlink dish and router both send test pings to the internet many times per minute. Latency measures how long, in milliseconds, a request takes to go to the internet and back. High latency may impact your experience with online gaming, video calls, and web browsing. It may be caused by extreme weather or periods of high network usage.
metrics.pingExplainer: Starlink and the Starlink router both send test pings to the internet many times per minute. It is normal for a few pings to drop without your connection noticeably suffering. Sustained dips are what matter, and they line up with the outages marked on the chart.
metrics.powerExplainer: Power draw is how much electricity the Starlink terminal is using. It rises under heavy load and when the dish heats itself to melt snow or ice.
metrics.searchingHelp: Dishylink talks to your Starlink terminal directly at <address>{{address}}</address>. Make sure this machine is connected to the Starlink network (Wi‑Fi or ethernet behind the Starlink router) and that the dish is powered. Retrying automatically…

wanEthPoorConnection.firing: Poor Ethernet connection to the dish

highCablePingDropRate.advice: Check the Starlink cable and its connections at both ends.

thermalThrottle.firing: Router is hot and is slowing Wi-Fi to cool down

meshUnreliableBackhaul.firing: Mesh nodes have an unreliable link to the router

meshTopologyChangingOften.firing: Mesh nodes keep switching how they connect

lanEthSlowLink10.firing: A LAN port is stuck at 10 Mbps

lanEthSlowLink100.firing: A LAN port is capped at 100 Mbps

wiredMeshNotUsingWanIface.ok: Wired mesh on the right port
wiredMeshNotUsingWanIface.firing: Wired mesh node is not using its WAN port

poeOffCurrentNominal.firing: Power supply is off but still drawing current

freshlyFused.firing: Router is freshly fused and not yet set up

dishUnreachable.advice: Check that the dish has power and that its cable to the router is seated at both ends.

starlinkOutage.ok: Pings to the Starlink network are succeeding again
starlinkOutage.firing: The dish is reachable, but pings to the Starlink network are failing
starlinkOutage.advice: Nothing on your side is wrong. Heavy weather or a gap in satellite coverage will clear on its own.

recorderOff.firing: Recording was off — anything in this gap went unrecorded

historianDown.firing: History recorder is down — live alerts still work, but nothing is being recorded

eventDetail.title: Event details
eventDetail.noReport: The history recorder did not time this event, so there are no figures for it.

events.title: Events & outages
events.empty: no outages recorded in the current window

NO_PINGS.label: Ping Network Interruption
NO_PINGS.tip: Radio frequency link looked fine but pings to the ground station/POP failed — traffic wasn't actually flowing.

NO_DOWNLINK.label: Downlink Network Interruption
NO_DOWNLINK.tip: Dish was pointed at a satellite but received no decodable downlink signal.

NO_SATS.label: No satellite in range
NO_SATS.tip: No Starlink satellite was overhead to connect to.

NO_SCHEDULE.label: No service scheduled
NO_SCHEDULE.tip: Network gave your cell no time slot (seen during network congestion, service issues, account problems, or right after boot before a schedule downloads).

OBSTRUCTED.label: Dish's view obstructed
OBSTRUCTED.tip: Something physically blocked the dish's view of the sky (branch, roof, pole), so it dropped the satellite.

THERMAL_SHUTDOWN.label: Overheated
THERMAL_SHUTDOWN.tip: The dish's internal temperature exceeded safe limits (hot climate + direct sun) and it shut down to cool off.

RAIN_SNR_PERSISTENTLY_LOW.label: Weather interference
RAIN_SNR_PERSISTENTLY_LOW.tip: Heavy rain/snow degraded signal-to-noise below usable level.

WEAK_SIGNAL_FROM_WEATHER.label: Weather interference
WEAK_SIGNAL_FROM_WEATHER.tip: Heavy rain/snow degraded signal-to-noise below usable level.

SKY_SEARCH.label: Searching for satellites
SKY_SEARCH.tip: Dish was scanning the sky to lock onto satellites (after boot or being moved).

ACTUATOR_ACTIVITY.label: Repositioning
ACTUATOR_ACTIVITY.tip: The dish's motors were physically moving it (repositioning/realigning); RF is muted while it moves.

STOWED.label: Dish stowed
STOWED.tip: Dish was folded in stow position.

SLEEPING.label: Scheduled sleep
SLEEPING.tip: Scheduled sleep window (the "snooze" schedule in the app).

CABLE_TEST.label: Cable test
CABLE_TEST.tip: Dish was running its cable diagnostic.

INHIBIT_RF.label: Transmission paused
INHIBIT_RF.tip: Dish stopped transmitting (RF inhibited — for safety, or commanded off).

ROUTER_POWER_CYCLE.label: Router powered on
ROUTER_POWER_CYCLE.tip: The router lost and regained power (unplugged/replugged, or a power blip).

CLIENT_SWITCHING_BAND.label: Device switched WiFi band
CLIENT_SWITCHING_BAND.tip: A device switched Wi-Fi bands. This is normal when devices are optimizing their Wi-Fi performance, but may cause a brief interruption.

ETH_NO_LINK.label: Ethernet cable link to dish disconnected
ETH_NO_LINK.tip: The ethernet link between the router and the dish went dead. Expected for a few seconds while either device reboots; at any other time, check the cable at both ends.

ROUTER_POP_IPV4_PING_DROP.label: Router lost its keepalive ping (IPv4)
ROUTER_POP_IPV4_PING_DROP.tip: The router's own ping to the ground station went unanswered. It watches the link with these pings; losing them means the path looked unhealthy to the router, not that your traffic stopped — data usually keeps flowing right through it.

ROUTER_POP_IPV6_PING_DROP.label: Router lost its keepalive ping (IPv6)
ROUTER_POP_IPV6_PING_DROP.tip: As the IPv4 drop, on the IPv6 path. Seen alone it usually means only IPv6 was affected, which most traffic can route around.

ROUTER_DISH_PING_DROP.label: Router lost contact with the dish briefly
ROUTER_DISH_PING_DROP.tip: The router's keepalive ping to the dish over the Ethernet cable went unanswered. Expected while the dish reboots; otherwise it points at the cable between them.

HIGH_DOWNLINK_PACKET_LOSS.label: Elevated packet loss
HIGH_DOWNLINK_PACKET_LOSS.tip: A raised share of incoming packets was lost. The connection stayed up — this is quality degrading, not service stopping.

CLIENT_SWITCHING_UPSTREAM_MAC.label: Device moved to another access point
CLIENT_SWITCHING_UPSTREAM_MAC.tip: A connected device handed off between the router and a mesh node, or between radios.

ROUTER_PUBLIC_IPV4_CHANGE.label: Public IP address changed
ROUTER_PUBLIC_IPV4_CHANGE.tip: Starlink issued the router a different public IPv4 address — normal on a CGNAT network.

desktop.notificationsUndeliverable: macOS isn’t delivering notifications — allow Dishylink under System Settings ▸ Notifications.
desktop.notificationsDevRun: Native notifications need the installed Dishylink app; a dev run can’t post them.
